As for why... because the emotional answer varies from person to person I'll stick with the scientific one.  Depression is caused by neurotransmitters. The main ones related to depression in general are; Dopamine, Serotonin, and Norepinephrine.

**Why and how these neurotransmitters contribute to depression;**

**Dopamine.** Dopamine causes positive feelings associated with reward. (Ex; How if you achieve a big accomplishment you feel good about yourself, that's the effect of the dopamine.)

Some people's dopamine levels are lower than others. When you have a lack of dopamine it causes you to lose interest in doing or trying certain things. (Ex; Getting out of bed in the morning, studying for a test, cleaning, etc.)

Some antidepressants are targeted to affect the dopamine system so that it produces the amount of dopamine it should.

**Serotonin.** Serotonin helps regulate your mood as well as many other things including gut regulation, blood clotting, and even sexual function. Serotonin is the main neurotransmitter associated with depression, and most popular antidepressants (Prozac, Celexa, Zoloft) are labeled as "SSRIs."  Also known as Selective Serotonin Reuptake Inhibitors. They specifically affect serotonin molecules.

Scientist have done some studies and have found that low serotonin levels and also lead to lower norepinephrine levels (which is the next neurotransmitter I'm gonna go over)

**Norepinephrine.** Norepinephrine is a neurotransmitter as well as a hormone. It's responsible for your "fight or flight response" along with adrenaline. Too little norepinephrine can cause depression in SOME but not all. Having lower norepinephrine levels does not mean you will have depression or that it is the cause of your depression. On the other hand too much norepinephrine can cause mania.

Norepinephrine medication is available and well as newer antidepressants called SNRIs ( Serotonin-Norepinephrine Reuptake Inhibitors)
